principles.statement: Preserve an uninterrupted first pass whenever natural-flow listening evidence is the target and the clip is within readiness bounds.
Treat learner pause/replay as a repair affordance, not as evidence-free UI; record every temporal intervention and exposure count.
Use paused transcription or similarly bounded tasks to diagnose local decoding/segmentation failure after a breakdown rather than chopping every listening task by default.
Keep continuous, learner-paused, system-paused and segmented-repair successes as distinct evidence states.
Do not auto-pause every sentence or predicted unknown word; trigger system interruption only for an explicit diagnostic/repair objective.
When system pausing is used, preserve boundary provenance because pause placement changes the linguistic signal and can interact with proficiency.
Prefer the smallest temporal repair that resolves the detected breakdown, then return the learner to continuous playback.
Learner-controlled playback should remain available and obvious; train purposeful use when behavior shows indiscriminate or absent control use.
Automated difficult-segment replay/slowdown is a candidate repair mechanism, not proof of improved independent listening.
Validate any automated pause trigger as a classifier with false-positive, false-negative and subgroup performance, not only end-task average score.
Do not infer a universal pause duration or frequency from general multimedia or older input-modification studies.
Use Vietnamese beginner evidence to justify direct calibration of prosody/temporal-support policies, not to claim that auto-pause itself has been validated for this population.

Ship system-triggered pausing only if EXP-011 shows better delayed unseen continuous listening or equal learning with materially lower time/effort without unacceptable dependence or false interruptions.
